Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Samoa's reply with the bat. The umpires and players are out in the middle. Now, the fielders of Pakistan Women Under-19 scatter out to their fielding positions. Out walk the Samoan opening pair of Norah Jade Salima and Verra Farane. Fatima Khan has the new ball for Pakistan and will begin the proceedings in the chase. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well then, an imposing total for Samoa Women Under-19 awaits when they come out to chase. Batting hasn't been their strongest suit and they would be challenged by the Pakistani bowling unit. This marks an opportunity for Somoa to show some fight and end their tournament on a positive note. For Pakistan Women Under-19, they would aim at snagging early wickets and give no chance to their opponents. An exciting run-chase up next shortly.

Maham Anees from Pakistan Women Under-19 is in for a chat. She says the pitch was wet and the bowlers were taking pace off which made it difficult to bat and she had to generate a lot of power. Mentions that she was very happy to open the innings and is happy to be representing the team. Concludes that she will look to get better with her strike rates going ahead.

Fatima Khan then stepped up in the final overs, delivering a quick cameo that propelled Pakistan's innings past 100. Particularly her impactful 20 runs in the 17th over provided the critical boost, but they again lost the momentum towards the fag end against Norah Jade Salima's double whammy. She eventually ended her stint with three wickets and was the most successful bowler for Samoa.

It wasn't that easy to score on a sluggish surface but Pakistan ensured that the scoring rate remains above run-a-ball. A pivotal partnership between Maham and Minahil in the middle overs helped stabilize the innings. They capitalized on Samoa's fielding lapses and benefited from additional extras. However, Pakistan's attempt to accelerate led to a dramatic middle-order collapse. Hasty running and loose shots saw them tumble from a relatively comfortable 66/2 to a precarious 83/5. Simultaneously, Samoa showed a gradual improvement, tightening their lines and lengths to slow down the scoring rate with two new batters.

Pakistan Women Under-19 had a decent start as skipper Komal Khan did strike a couple of boundaries first up to get things going but lost her wicket eventually in order to keep the momentum. Maham Anees looked a bit cagy in her approach but made sure that she stayed in the middle. However, Norah Jade Salima and skipper Avetia Fetu Mapu kept things tight from one end and a suicidal run out saw Pakistan reduced to 41/2 in the Powerplay.

So, 48 runs in the last five overs for Pakistan Women Under-19. They would be pleased as this is their highest score in this edition of the tournament. For Samoa Women Under-19, while they leaked runs, they can take pride in their bowling performance of dismissing 8 of Pakistan's batters.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities behind us, it's time for the action to take over. The two umpires make their way out to the middle and Samoa players burst open off their final huddle and spread across the field. Komal Khan and Maham Anees are the openers for Pakistan Women Under-19. Olive Lefaga Lemoe has the new ball and will start the proceedings. Here we go.
Out come the match officials and both sets of players for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Samoa first followed by that of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Isobel Joyce is down in the middle for the pitch analysis. She says pitch number 3 will be used for this game and the boundaries all around are 55 meters. Mentions that the outfield is very heavy due to overnight rain and both teams will have run well between the wickets considering they have struggled to find boundaries. Adds that the overhead conditions are dry as of now but there are possibilities of rain later. Says the pitch should suit spinners and this could be a low-scoring contest where 80-100 runs could prove to be match-winning.

Komal Khan, the captain of Pakistan Women Under-19 says that they would have bowled first as well, but now they will challenge the opposition with the bat. Adds that they are ready to put up a good performance in their final game of the tournament. Informs three changes in the side.

Avetia Fetu Mapu, the skipper of Samoa Women Under-19 says they just want to go out and enjoy their game and adds that it has been a fun ride thus far. Mentions that they have two changes in their side.

Samoa Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Norah Jade Salima, Verra Farane, Olive Lefaga Lemoe, Avetia Fetu Mapu (C), Stella Sagalala, Angel Sootaga So (WK), Stefania Pauga, Apolonia Polataivao (In for Jane Taliilagi Manase), Barbara Ella Keresoma, Katrina Uiese Taa Samu, Silepea Polataivao (In for Masina Tafea).

Pakistan Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Komal Khan (C/WK), Zoofishan Ayyaz, Fatima Khan, Areesha Ansari, Minahil, Maham Anees, Haniah Ahmer (In for Ravail Farhan), Quratulain, Tayyba Imdad, Shahar Bano (In for Memoona Khalid), Wasifa Hussain (In for Mahnoor Zeb).
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in the favor of Samoa Women Under-19 and they have elected to BOWL first.

Facing overwhelming challenges in a group with cricket powerhouses like New Zealand and South Africa, the Samoa Women Under-19 team has faced tremendous examination. Their tournament journey, characterized by low scores of 16 and 40, might appear discouraging on the surface. However, these experiences represent an invaluable learning curve for this emerging cricketing nation. Their bowling unit, particularly Olive Lefaga Lemoe and Verra Farane, showed promising potential against New Zealand. For a developing cricket nation like Samoa, such tournaments are not measured solely by wins and losses, but by the developmental opportunities they create. Will they challenge Pakistan this time around and win a consolation? Stay tuned for the toss and team updates.

Pakistan's tournament journey was fraught with difficulties, as they failed to secure a single victory in their three group matches. Their campaign was marked by losses to England Women and a surprising defeat against Ireland Women in a rain-shortened game. A complete washout against USA Women further complicated their path. The team's primary struggle came from batting collapses, though their bowlers showed glimpses of resilience. Notable performers like Mahnoor Zeb, Fatima Khan, and Memoona Khalid provided some hope by contributing meaningful wickets.

Hello and a very warm welcome to our coverage as we bring you the 4th Place Playoff clash in the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025. It is Match number 1 in this phase of the tournament where the two teams that finished in the fourth place of Group B and C, respectively will meet. It will be Pakistan Women Under-19 going up against Samoa Women Under-19 at the Johar Cricket Academy Oval.
... MATCH DAY ...

With the top 12 teams advancing to the Super Six stage, the remaining teams, who finished last in their respective groups, now face off in the 4th Place Playoff to determine their final standings in the competition. The first of these playoffs takes place at the Johor Cricket Academy Oval, where Pakistan Women Under-19 will take on Samoa Women Under-19, with both sides eager to finish their campaign on a positive note. Both Pakistan and Samoa endured challenging campaigns. Pakistan Women Under-19 shared points in their rain-washed opening game but lost their next two matches, leaving them winless in the tournament. Their struggles were highlighted by a shocking loss to Ireland Women in a rain-shortened 9-over game, where they failed to chase a target of 70 runs. While Pakistan’s bowlers have shown glimpses of promise, their batting and fielding have let them down time and again. No batter has stepped up to anchor the innings, with wickets often falling in heaps, a formula that has consistently derailed their chances. This match presents Pakistan with an opportunity to salvage some pride and bring an otherwise forgettable season to a close. Samoa Women Under-19, meanwhile, entered the tournament as the first team to qualify from the regional pathway through the East Asia-Pacific Qualifier. After their first game was washed out, their inexperience showed against two of the strongest teams in world cricket, they gained valuable lessons along the way. Their most promising performance came in their final group match against New Zealand, where the bowlers shone brightly. Olive Lefaga Lemoe was the standout, claiming 3 wickets, while Verra Farane and the rest of the bowling unit chipped in to claim 9 Kiwi batters in total which is a remarkable effort against a powerhouse side. While Pakistan Women Under-19 may appear to be the favourites on paper, Samoa Women Under-19 will draw confidence from their last performance and aim to exploit Pakistan’s lack of confidence and momentum. This match has the potential to be a fiercely competitive battle as both teams look to end their campaigns on a high note.
